findings.evidence: 7 of 7 sampled 2xx product pages carry noindex or none in their robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag header (100%). A page excluded from the index cannot be retrieved into an answer.
exceptions_checked: editorial noindex on single pages: at least 2 pages and 50% of the type required
syndicated copies pointing elsewhere by canonical: excluded
false_positive_controls_applied: 2xx pages only
exact token match after lower-casing
X-Robots-Tag scopes other than the retrieval crawlers ignored
pages declaring another URL as canonical excluded
category, contact, policy and other pages never counted

suggested_action.how: Find the template or SEO-plugin setting that applies the directive to the whole type, often a 'discourage indexing' toggle left on from staging, and scope it to the pages actually meant to be excluded.
suggested_action.mechanism: Index admission for the affected template.
suggested_action.success_criteria: A plain fetch of every cited URL returns no noindex or none in either the robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag.
suggested_action.summary: Remove noindex from the product template or the header rule that emits it.
suggested_action.what: Remove noindex (or none) from the product page template, or from the header rule adding it.
suggested_action.where: The robots meta tag in the product template or the server/CDN rule setting X-Robots-Tag, on the URLs cited.
suggested_action.why: The directive is applied after fetching, so no amount of crawl access recovers the page.

findings.evidence: The same client sent the same request with different user-agent strings: browser-ua received 2xx, while GPTBot received a refusal (GPTBot: 403 on http://127.0.0.1:58918/, 403 on http://127.0.0.1:58918/pages/about-us). robots.txt admits these agents. This compares two header strings, not a browser against a crawler, and cannot show how requests from the operators' own addresses are treated.
exceptions_checked: edge verification of claimed identity by published address ranges: indistinguishable here, so status is risk at low confidence
false_positive_controls_applied: 429 and 5xx excluded
Googlebot excluded: refusing unverified Googlebot is documented defence
not fired when Googlebot was refused on the same URLs, the pattern of verification by address
refusal required on every URL where browser-ua received 2xx
agents robots.txt disallows are never probed

suggested_action.how: Filter logs for the crawler's user-agent string, compare source addresses against the operator's published ranges, and check the status verified requests received; if refused, verify identity by address instead of refusing by string.
suggested_action.mechanism: Admission of the crawler where the policy already grants it.
suggested_action.success_criteria: Server logs show 2xx responses to requests from the crawler's published address ranges on the cited URLs.
suggested_action.summary: Check the server logs for how verified requests from the named crawlers are answered.
suggested_action.what: Establish whether requests from the named crawler's published address ranges receive 2xx, and if not, remove the user-agent match refusing them.
suggested_action.where: Server access logs first, then web server, CDN bot-management or firewall rules matching on User-Agent.
suggested_action.why: robots.txt admits these crawlers, so a refusal at the server contradicts the site's own policy.

findings.title: A named AI crawler identity is refused where robots.txt admits it

suggested_action.how: Generate offers.price from the same variable that renders the visible price, including sale and selected-variant logic, rather than from a separate field.

findings.evidence: This audit observes the site, not assistants' answers, by design. 1 claim was promoted with at least medium first-party confidence, which gives a panel whose expected answers are known: What is northwind threads, and what is its official website? (expected: 127.0.0.1).

suggested_action.how: Use exactly these prompts each time, record date, assistant, answer and whether it matches: What is northwind threads, and what is its official website? (expected: 127.0.0.1). Re-run after each fix from this report to see whether it moved anything.
suggested_action.mechanism: Turns the audit's fixes into something whose effect can be seen.
suggested_action.success_criteria: A dated record of answers per assistant exists, and each answer is marked as matching or not matching the site's stated value.
suggested_action.summary: Ask the same questions of the main assistants monthly and record whether each answer matches the site.
suggested_action.what: Run a fixed panel of questions about northwind threads against the assistants that matter to the site, on a schedule, and record each answer against the expected value.
suggested_action.where: Outside the site: a shared sheet or a scheduled script owned by whoever owns the brand's facts.
suggested_action.why: Whether a fix changes what assistants say is not observable from the site, so it has to be measured where it happens.

findings.title: Monitor how assistants describe northwind threads with a fixed prompt panel

findings.evidence: /llms.txt at http://127.0.0.1:58918 answered HTTP 404 and is not present. No major assistant is documented to read this file, so this is listed only as a low-cost hedge, not as a gap.

suggested_action.how: Write a short markdown file: one paragraph describing the organization, then links to the pages that answer the questions people ask about it. Keep it consistent with those pages.
suggested_action.mechanism: A possible, undocumented discovery channel for tools that adopt the convention.
suggested_action.success_criteria: /llms.txt answers 200 with content that is not the site's soft-404 page.
suggested_action.summary: If it costs little, publish a short /llms.txt; do not expect it to change how assistants see the site.
suggested_action.what: Publish a plain-text /llms.txt summarising what the site is and linking its key pages.
suggested_action.why: It is a proposed convention some tools read; no major assistant documents consuming it, which is why this is proactive and never a finding.

findings.title: Optional and speculative: publish /llms.txt

findings.evidence: 2 of 14 sampled URLs (14%), all discovered from the site's own sitemap, navigation or links, returned an error: 404 http://127.0.0.1:58918/products/retired-logo-tee, 404 http://127.0.0.1:58918/products/retired-classic-tee.
exceptions_checked: retired content served 410 behind a stale link: counted, the reference is the defect
false_positive_controls_applied: 401, 403 and 429 excluded as refusals to this client
status judged at the final URL after redirects
5xx lowers confidence

suggested_action.how: For each cited URL restore the page, add a 301 to its current equivalent, or remove it from the sitemap and linking template; for 5xx, check application logs for the failing route.
suggested_action.success_criteria: A plain fetch of every cited URL returns 2xx, a redirect to a 2xx, or the URL no longer appears in the sitemap or on linking pages.
suggested_action.summary: Stop advertising URLs that do not resolve; restore or redirect the ones that should.
suggested_action.what: Restore, redirect, or stop linking the cited URLs.
suggested_action.where: The sitemap generator and the navigation or link templates that produced the cited URLs.
suggested_action.why: Each reference sends crawlers to an error and spends crawl they would otherwise use on real pages.
